name: Tetramethylammonium hydroxide
description: Tetramethylammonium hydroxide ( CAS 75-59-2 ), commonly abbreviated as TMAH, is a quaternary ammonium base used across semiconductor manufacturing, pharmaceutical synthesis, and analytical chemistry. It functions as a strong, metal-free alkali, making it the preferred choice where inorganic base contamination is unacceptable. In semiconductor and flat-panel display manufacturing, it is the standard developer. TMAH is used for photoresist stripping and patterning, where its metal-free profile prevents ionic contamination of wafer surfaces. Pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturers use it as a catalyst and pH-adjusting agent. It is ideal for synthesis steps that require a clean base without introducing sodium or potassium ions. In analytical laboratories, it is used as a quaternizing agent for GC sample preparation. This enables direct injection of fatty acid and biological samples. It also supports etching of silicon wafers in MEMS fabrication, where precise anisotropic etch rates are critical to device geometry. TMAH is supplied as aqueous solution, most commonly at 25% concentration, with lower concentrations such as 5% and 10% available for specific process requirements. Pentahydrate solid form is also available. Electronic-grade and reagent-grade specifications are the primary market grades.
